tagline: Attach Loom video walkthroughs to Linear issues for richer async context
metaTitle: Linear + Loom Integration: Loom Bug Recordings to Issues
metaDescription: Turn Loom bug recordings into Linear issues and add sprint demos to finished issues. GAIA keeps video context on work. See the setup steps.
intro:
Text descriptions in Linear issues often fall short for complex bugs or nuanced feature feedback. A ten-second Loom recording of a UI bug conveys more than three paragraphs of written description — but attaching that recording to the right issue requires remembering the issue number, opening Linear, and manually pasting the video link.

GAIA connects the two. When a Loom recording is created with a specific tag or title convention, GAIA identifies the relevant issue and attaches the video automatically. Bug recordings generate new issues with the video embedded. Sprint update videos are posted as comments on all issues completed that week.

For remote and async-first dev teams, this integration enables a richer asynchronous communication layer on top of the structured issue workflow — combining the precision of issue tracking with the clarity of video communication.

useCases.title: Bug recording to Linear issue
useCases.description: When a QA tester or user records a Loom showing a bug, GAIA creates an issue with the video embedded as the primary description, making it immediately actionable for the assigned engineer.

useCases.title: Design feedback videos on issues
useCases.description: Designers record walkthroughs of design feedback and GAIA attaches them to the corresponding Linear implementation issues so engineers see the exact changes requested without a meeting.

useCases.title: Sprint demo recordings on completed issues
useCases.description: After a sprint demo, GAIA attaches the recording to each issue demonstrated, creating a permanent video record of what was built and how it works.

useCases.title: Async standup updates
useCases.description: Engineers record daily standup updates mentioning their issues. GAIA parses the video transcript and posts relevant updates as comments on each mentioned issue.

useCases.title: Onboarding walkthroughs linked to issues
useCases.description: GAIA attaches relevant onboarding and architecture walkthrough videos to issues in specific areas, giving new engineers video context alongside written issue descriptions.

howItWorks.step: Connect Linear and Loom to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate your Linear workspace and your video workspace in GAIA's settings. GAIA uses Loom's API to access video metadata and transcripts.
Tell GAIA how to identify which videos relate to which issues, by title convention (e.g., including the issue ID), by folder, or by transcript content analysis.

howItWorks.step: GAIA links videos to issues automatically
howItWorks.description: When a new video is created matching your rules, GAIA attaches it to the appropriate issue as a comment or description link and notifies the relevant team member.

faqs.question: Can GAIA create a Linear issue from a Loom recording without a pre-existing issue?
faqs.answer: Yes. If a recording title includes a trigger phrase (e.g., 'Bug:' or 'Issue:'), GAIA creates a new issue using the video title as the issue name and embeds the link as the description.

faqs.question: Does GAIA use transcripts to populate issue fields?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA reads the transcript to extract a summary, steps to reproduce (for bugs), and any mentioned issue numbers, using this content to populate the issue description and comments.

faqs.question: Does the viewer need an account to watch an attached recording?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Videos can be set to public or shared-link access. GAIA attaches videos using their shared link so anyone with the issue can view the recording without logging in to the video service.

faqs.question: Can GAIA attach videos to sub-issues or just top-level issues?
faqs.answer: GAIA can attach links to both top-level issues and sub-issues. This is particularly useful for QA feedback on specific acceptance criteria tracked as sub-issues.
